S1 BLOCKING — Name extraction deduplicates identities by discarding distinct retrieval reasons.
Invariant/authority: D1 requires each matching name/key to carry its matchedName and ambiguity reason; AC3 preserves multiple meaningful retrieval reasons. ADR 0020 section 5 step 4 and integrated transition design sections 6.2/7.1 require merging identities while preserving every meaningful retrieval reason. Failed stage: signal extraction; affected owner is runtime discovery.
Location: packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:198 (key-only seen guard); canonical-discovery disposition at docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json:309 overstates closure.
Concrete scenario: real bundled stack, playerInput='I know spellbook and cantrips', empty state. feature:wizard:spellcasting is indexed by BOTH section names. The cantrips signal marks its key seen; the later spellbook match emits no signal for it. Its retained/rendered packet carries only matchedName=cantrips, missing the spellbook route and ambiguity with equipment:spellbook. ambiguousNames still records spellbook, but that observation is not a substitute for the candidate's packet route.
Sibling/state analysis: 'Spellcasting Ability' loses that reason for seven Spellcasting feature keys because the shorter spellcasting name wins first; 'Spellcasting Focus' loses it for six feature keys. Reversing the real feature byName map changes which reason survives. Reversing player word order does not repair 'Spellbook Cantrips'. Adding a state reference adds a direct-state-ref route but does not restore the lost name route. Candidates, expansion, dedup, retention, packet, projection and shadow carry emitted evidence generically; the loss is upstream. M3 reports no lost routes because it measures routes after extraction, so existing green probes do not distinguish this bad state.
Closure: preserve independently meaningful matched-name/key reasons with their own correct sibling sets while keeping one canonical candidate identity; verify they survive into rendered packets and durable trace projection, update registry reasoning, and check the effect on route-count ranking/retention without silently changing policy.
Permanent evidence: a generalized invariant over overlapping indexed names and independently derived expected name/key reasons, with real section-alias/nested-name examples and index-order variation; assert both signal and packet evidence. This small boundary check is proportionate to losing DM relevance/disambiguation evidence; no universal retrieval proof is required.
Repair material: YES — it changes signal/route multiplicity or evidence semantics, potentially route-count ranking and durable discovery evidence. Fresh full review of the repaired affected scope is required.

S2 BLOCKING — D2 claims source-qualified ambiguous lookup summaries that the tool never returns.
Invariant/authority: owning bead DESIGN D2 explicitly requires every DM consumer showing a colliding name to include kind and source, naming lookup_rules candidate summaries and packet rendering; qualify a consumer where this is absent. Review policy requires dispositions to rely on actual consumer evidence.
Location: docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json:296; actual unqualified branch packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolLookupRules.ts:176-180. RulesRecordCard is emitted only by the successful branch at line 161.
Concrete scenario: directly invoking the real lookupRulesTool with {kind:'rule', name:'Darkvision', systemId:'dnd5e-srd'} returns an ambiguous message and data={candidateKeys:['rule:darkvision','rule:senses-darkvision']}. Neither source nor locator accompanies those candidates, despite their distinct SRD passages at pp.86/257. The registry states that RulesRecordCard is used for ambiguous results; that is false. The DM must issue further lookups just to learn the candidate sources D2 requires in this presentation.
Sibling/state analysis: actual tool invocations for feature Spellcasting and Ability Score Improvement show the same keys-only response. The common ambiguous branch affects all same-kind name/section-alias collisions, including custom/add-on stacks; successful lookups and packet candidateBlock already supply kind/source and need no equivalent repair. Preserve the existing candidate-key cap and explicit overflow behavior.
Closure: provide kind/source-qualified summaries for the candidates actually shown in ambiguous tool results using the resolved winning entries; retain candidateKeys/re-query behavior and correct the F-22 registry disposition to cite the real boundary.
Permanent evidence: a generalized ambiguous-tool-output contract test checking each shown candidate's identity and source/locator against its resolved entry, covering source-distinct rule passages and same-kind feature collisions; proportionate to a live DM tool contract, without requiring a separate test for the card helper.
Repair material: YES — it changes the live model-facing ambiguous tool-output contract and its D2 disposition; requires fresh review of the affected producer/consumer boundary.

S3 BLOCKING — Exact punctuated ambiguous names still lose every name-mention route.
Invariant/authority: D1 repairs the ambiguous-name route class, and current AC4 admits demonstrated missing discovery routes. Integrated transition design section 6.2 defines explicit-name-or-alias as player text containing an exact record name or indexed alias. This is a positive, represented-name contract, not universal semantic retrieval completeness.
Location: packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:150-152 and :175-181; input punctuation is replaced with spaces while indexed rawName is compared unchanged.
Concrete scenario: playerInput='I use Land’s Stride' (also straight apostrophe) with empty state emits no name signal, candidate or retained packet for feature:circle-of-the-land:lands-stride or feature:ranger:lands-stride. Both exact printed names exist in the real byName index and vendored PDF pp.22/37. Input becomes 'land s stride', which matches neither indexed "land's stride" nor apostrophe-free 'lands stride'. 'I use Lands Stride' surfaces both, demonstrating the asymmetric normalization.
Sibling/state analysis: audited every cross-kind-unioned colliding byName entry: 89 indexed name groups. Three indexed spellings lose their expected keys: land's stride; food, drink, and lodging; and its existing comma-reordered alias drink, and lodging food. The latter two both miss rule:food-drink-and-lodging and table:food-drink-and-lodging (PDF p.73). Literal 'Food, Drink, and Lodging' retrieves only unrelated rule:food. The other 86 groups retain their expected identities with no budget overflow; no emitted route is lost downstream. Adding a direct state reference can surface one Land's Stride identity through that independent route but leaves the named route absent. This normalization defect predates the diff but remains inside the declared ambiguous-name discovery scope and cannot be discharged by CAP-011 reasoning.
Closure: align input/index matching for represented punctuation and aliases, preserving word boundaries, stable identities and correct ambiguity siblings; close the demonstrated punctuation class and update discovery disposition evidence. No invented alias table, pack-text rewrite or new semantic ranker is required.
Permanent evidence: a generalized input/index normalization invariant with the source-backed same-kind apostrophe and cross-kind comma examples; independently enumerate expected keys from the existing index and confirm candidates/packet presence. A small representative boundary test is proportionate to losing all routes for a known name.
Repair material: YES — it changes name-recognition and ambiguity semantics, so fresh review of the affected discovery scope is required.

NOT A FINDING — No requirement to add a universal ontology, alias table, global retrieval-completeness gate, or tests for every proof helper.
